# Code Map — Dispatcher (Admin Web App / Dispatch Console)

Next.js 16 / React 19, frontend-only prototype on mock data. components/Console.tsx is the
shell (TopBar + NavRail + screen switch, state in lib/nav.ts). Styling is inline style
objects driven by lib/theme.ts tokens — no Tailwind/CSS modules.

- fleet/DefectsPanel.tsx is one component rendered on four surfaces (trip detail, CreateTripWizard, the vehicle's Open Defects tab, and its ResolveDefectModal alone from InspectionDetailModal) — WARN-ONLY by design: it reports nothing to its parent, so no mount point can quietly become a block on trip creation or vehicle assignment.
- ui/Chip.tsx StatusChip takes an optional `glyph` to separate two states that share one protected colour (a defect's Major and Out-of-Service are both vermillion) — an extra icon, never a new colour.
<!-- notes:dispatcher-components:end -->

<!-- notes:dispatcher-lib:start -->
- data.ts holds ALL mock data (the API seam — never invent endpoint shapes) · types.ts entity types · theme.ts color/typography tokens (extend it, no ad hoc colors) · nav.ts screen-switch state.
- billing/accruals.ts and reports/terminus.ts are the pure period→figures report derivations; the screen, the printed sheet (documents/accrualsPdf, documents/terminusPdf) and the clipboard export all consume them rather than recompute.
- claims.ts decodes the JWT payload WITHOUT signature verification — deliberate UX gate, not a security boundary (the API validates every request); claim names couple to Identity's JwtAccessTokenIssuer.cs, and Budgeting/lib/claims.ts is a twin that must stay in step.
<!-- notes:dispatcher-lib:end -->
